1	# Integrating guessless into an agent workflow
2	
3	This is the adoption guide: how to put guessless in front of an agent that is about to claim it
4	renamed every call site, and how to make that claim mechanically checkable later.
5	
6	It has four layers. They are not alternatives — they escalate, and only the bottom two enforce
7	anything.
8	
9	| Layer | File | What it does | Does it enforce? |
10	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
11	| 1. Docs | `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` | Tells the agent the tool exists and when to reach for it | No |
12	| 2. Skill | `.claude/skills/guessless/SKILL.md` | Loads the how-to on demand, so the agent does not have to remember the envelope shapes | No |
13	| 3. Stop hook | `.claude/settings.json` | Refuses to let a turn end on an unpriced completeness claim | **Yes, in the loop** |
14	| 4. CI | your workflow file | Re-runs every committed receipt and fails the build if one does not reproduce | **Yes, at merge** |
15	
16	Read the [adoption facts](#adoption-facts-what-is-actually-measured) before deciding how much of
17	this to install. The short version: layers 1 and 2 are documentation, and documentation has never
18	been measured to make an agent pick this tool up on its own.
19	
20	---
21	
22	## Layer 1 — the docs block
23	
24	Paste this into the target repository's `AGENTS.md` (or `CLAUDE.md`). It is deliberately short:
25	long tool documentation competes with the task for attention.
26	
27	```markdown
28	## Structural claims about JavaScript/TypeScript
29	
30	Do not assert that you have found *all* call sites, *every* reference, or that a symbol is safe to
31	delete, unless you can show a guessless receipt for that exact claim. `grep` cannot see re-exports,
32	aliased imports, `export * from`, or property access through a namespace object, so "all" derived
33	from a text search is a guess.
34	
35	To price a completeness claim:
36	
37	    node <guessless>/packages/cli/dist/cli.js query envelope.json
38	
39	where `envelope.json` is `{"inputs": [{"path": "...", "source": "..."}], "request": {...}}`. The
40	answer is a receipt whose `state` is one of:
41	
42	- `complete` — the result set is exhaustive. This is the only state that licenses the word "all".
43	- `partial` — plus a named `unresolved` site for every place the engine could not classify. Say the
44	  answer is partial and name the gaps.
45	- `refused` — the question was not answered. It supports no claim at all.
46	
47	If you have no receipt, say which sites you checked instead of saying "all". A qualified answer is
48	always acceptable; an unpriced "all" is not.
49	```
50	
51	Replace `<guessless>` with the absolute path to your guessless checkout, or drop the path entirely
52	if guessless is installed as a dependency and `guessless` is on `PATH`.
53	
54	---
55	
56	## Layer 2 — the skill
57	
58	A skill keeps the envelope shapes out of the main context until they are needed. Create
59	`.claude/skills/guessless/SKILL.md` in the target repository:
60	
61	````markdown
62	---
63	name: guessless
64	description: Prove structural claims about JavaScript/TypeScript with a guessless receipt. Use when about to say "all call sites", "every reference", "nothing else imports this", or "safe to delete"; when renaming or deleting an exported symbol; when a claim gate has blocked a turn asking for a receipt; or when auditing whether a change is complete. Do not use for non-JS/TS languages.
65	---
66	
67	# Proving a structural claim with guessless
68	
69	Guessless answers reference/definition/reachability questions about JavaScript and TypeScript and
70	returns a signed receipt that is either exhaustive or explicitly incomplete. It never returns a bare
71	list, so every answer is either usable as proof or self-labelled as a gap.
72	
73	## 1. Build the query envelope
74	
75	Guessless is hermetic: it reads sources out of the envelope, not off disk. That is what makes a
76	receipt reproducible later.
77	
78	```json
79	{
80	  "inputs": [{ "path": "src/storage.ts", "source": "<file contents>" }],
81	  "request": { "kind": "exportedNames", "file": "src/storage.ts" }
82	}
83	```
84	
85	Include every file that could plausibly reference the symbol. A file you leave out is not a file
86	guessless says is clean — it is a file guessless never saw.
87	
88	Request kinds:
89	
90	| Kind | Fields | Answers |
91	| --- | --- | --- |
92	| `referencesOf` | `target` (symbol anchor) | Every reference to a symbol |
93	| `definitionOf` | `target` | Where a symbol is defined |
94	| `readsOf` / `writesOf` | `target` | Reads or writes of a binding |
95	| `capturesOf` | `target` | Closures capturing a binding |
96	| `reachableFrom` / `reaches` | `target` | Call-graph reachability |
97	| `exportedNames` | `file` | The module's export surface |
98	| `resolveBinding` | `file`, `name`, `space`, optional `scope` | What a name resolves to |
99	
100	Get a symbol anchor from an `exportedNames` or `definitionOf` receipt and pass it back verbatim —
101	anchors are fingerprinted, so hand-editing one invalidates it.
102	
103	## 2. Run it
104	
105	```bash
106	node <guessless>/packages/cli/dist/cli.js query envelope.json > answer.receipt.json
107	```
108	
109	## 3. Read the receipt honestly
110	
111	- `"state": "complete"` — say "all", and paste or cite the receipt.
112	- `"state": "partial"` — every place the engine could not classify is named in `unresolved`. Say the
113	  answer is partial, give the count, and name the gaps. Do not round a partial up to "all".
114	- `"state": "refused"` — `reason` and `detail` say why. Do not claim anything; fix the cause (often a
115	  non-JS/TS file) and re-query.
116	
117	## 4. Make it checkable
118	
119	Write the receipt beside a reproduction bundle so CI can re-run it:
120	
121	```
122	answer.receipt.json         the receipt
123	answer.reproduction.json    {"inputs": [...same inputs...], "receipt": {...that receipt...}}
124	```
125	
126	Then `node <guessless>/scripts/reproduce-check.mjs <dir>` re-runs it and fails if a single byte of
127	the receipt was altered.
128	
129	## Boundaries
130	
131	JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX and TSX only. Guessless has no opinion about other languages, about
132	runtime behaviour, or about whether a change is *correct* — only about whether a structural answer
133	is complete.
134	````
135	
136	The frontmatter is the whole trigger mechanism: `name` must match the directory, and `description`
137	must name the *conditions* under which to load the skill, because that description is all the agent
138	sees until it decides to open the file.
139	
140	---
141	
142	## Layer 3 — the Stop hook (the first layer that enforces)
143	
144	`scripts/claim-gate.mjs` is a Claude Code `Stop` hook. When a turn ends, it reads the last assistant
145	message out of the session transcript, looks for an unhedged structural completeness claim, and
146	blocks the stop if the claim has no receipt behind it.
147	
148	Add to the target repository's `.claude/settings.json`:
149	
150	```json
151	{
152	  "hooks": {
153	    "Stop": [
154	      {
155	        "hooks": [
156	          {
157	            "type": "command",
158	            "command": "node /Users/jacksm5pro/dev/open-source/guessless/scripts/claim-gate.mjs",
159	            "timeout": 10
160	          }
161	        ]
162	      }
163	    ]
164	  }
165	}

# Integrating guessless into an agent workflow

This is the adoption guide: how to put guessless in front of an agent that is about to claim it
renamed every call site, and how to make that claim mechanically checkable later.

It has four layers. They are not alternatives — they escalate, and only the bottom two enforce
anything.

| Layer | File | What it does | Does it enforce? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Docs | `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` | Tells the agent the tool exists and when to reach for it | No |
| 2. Skill | `.claude/skills/guessless/SKILL.md` | Loads the how-to on demand, so the agent does not have to remember the envelope shapes | No |
| 3. Stop hook | `.claude/settings.json` | Refuses to let a turn end on an unpriced completeness claim | **Yes, in the loop** |
| 4. CI | your workflow file | Re-runs every committed receipt and fails the build if one does not reproduce | **Yes, at merge** |

Read the [adoption facts](#adoption-facts-what-is-actually-measured) before deciding how much of
this to install. The short version: layers 1 and 2 are documentation, and documentation has never
been measured to make an agent pick this tool up on its own.

---

## Layer 1 — the docs block

Paste this into the target repository's `AGENTS.md` (or `CLAUDE.md`). It is deliberately short:
long tool documentation competes with the task for attention.

```markdown
## Structural claims about JavaScript/TypeScript

Do not assert that you have found *all* call sites, *every* reference, or that a symbol is safe to
delete, unless you can show a guessless receipt for that exact claim. `grep` cannot see re-exports,
aliased imports, `export * from`, or property access through a namespace object, so "all" derived
from a text search is a guess.

To price a completeness claim:

    node <guessless>/packages/cli/dist/cli.js query envelope.json

where `envelope.json` is `{"inputs": [{"path": "...", "source": "..."}], "request": {...}}`. The
answer is a receipt whose `state` is one of:

- `complete` — the result set is exhaustive. This is the only state that licenses the word "all".
- `partial` — plus a named `unresolved` site for every place the engine could not classify. Say the
  answer is partial and name the gaps.
- `refused` — the question was not answered. It supports no claim at all.

If you have no receipt, say which sites you checked instead of saying "all". A qualified answer is
always acceptable; an unpriced "all" is not.
```

Replace `<guessless>` with the absolute path to your guessless checkout, or drop the path entirely
if guessless is installed as a dependency and `guessless` is on `PATH`.

---

## Layer 2 — the skill

A skill keeps the envelope shapes out of the main context until they are needed. Create
`.claude/skills/guessless/SKILL.md` in the target repository:

````markdown
---
name: guessless
description: Prove structural claims about JavaScript/TypeScript with a guessless receipt. Use when about to say "all call sites", "every reference", "nothing else imports this", or "safe to delete"; when renaming or deleting an exported symbol; when a claim gate has blocked a turn asking for a receipt; or when auditing whether a change is complete. Do not use for non-JS/TS languages.
---

# Proving a structural claim with guessless

Guessless answers reference/definition/reachability questions about JavaScript and TypeScript and
returns a signed receipt that is either exhaustive or explicitly incomplete. It never returns a bare
list, so every answer is either usable as proof or self-labelled as a gap.

## 1. Build the query envelope

Guessless is hermetic: it reads sources out of the envelope, not off disk. That is what makes a
receipt reproducible later.

```json
{
  "inputs": [{ "path": "src/storage.ts", "source": "<file contents>" }],
  "request": { "kind": "exportedNames", "file": "src/storage.ts" }
}
```

Include every file that could plausibly reference the symbol. A file you leave out is not a file
guessless says is clean — it is a file guessless never saw.

Request kinds:

| Kind | Fields | Answers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `referencesOf` | `target` (symbol anchor) | Every reference to a symbol |
| `definitionOf` | `target` | Where a symbol is defined |
| `readsOf` / `writesOf` | `target` | Reads or writes of a binding |
| `capturesOf` | `target` | Closures capturing a binding |
| `reachableFrom` / `reaches` | `target` | Call-graph reachability |
| `exportedNames` | `file` | The module's export surface |
| `resolveBinding` | `file`, `name`, `space`, optional `scope` | What a name resolves to |

Get a symbol anchor from an `exportedNames` or `definitionOf` receipt and pass it back verbatim —
anchors are fingerprinted, so hand-editing one invalidates it.

## 2. Run it

```bash
node <guessless>/packages/cli/dist/cli.js query envelope.json > answer.receipt.json
```

## 3. Read the receipt honestly

- `"state": "complete"` — say "all", and paste or cite the receipt.
- `"state": "partial"` — every place the engine could not classify is named in `unresolved`. Say the
  answer is partial, give the count, and name the gaps. Do not round a partial up to "all".
- `"state": "refused"` — `reason` and `detail` say why. Do not claim anything; fix the cause (often a
  non-JS/TS file) and re-query.

## 4. Make it checkable

Write the receipt beside a reproduction bundle so CI can re-run it:

```
answer.receipt.json         the receipt
answer.reproduction.json    {"inputs": [...same inputs...], "receipt": {...that receipt...}}
```

Then `node <guessless>/scripts/reproduce-check.mjs <dir>` re-runs it and fails if a single byte of
the receipt was altered.

## Boundaries

JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX and TSX only. Guessless has no opinion about other languages, about
runtime behaviour, or about whether a change is *correct* — only about whether a structural answer
is complete.
````

The frontmatter is the whole trigger mechanism: `name` must match the directory, and `description`
must name the *conditions* under which to load the skill, because that description is all the agent
sees until it decides to open the file.

### Testing the gate without an agent

```bash

node /Users/jacksm5pro/dev/open-source/guessless/scripts/claim-gate.mjs --check /dev/null

# exits 2 — unpriced claim, reason on stderr

node /Users/jacksm5pro/dev/open-source/guessless/scripts/claim-gate.mjs --check claim.txt

# exits 0 — same claim, now priced
```

## Layer 4 — CI

The hook checks that a receipt was *cited*. CI checks that it is *true*.

`scripts/reproduce-check.mjs` walks a tree for `*.receipt.json` files, and for each one re-runs the
query through the built guessless CLI against the sources recorded in the sibling

```yaml
- name: Verify guessless receipts
  run: |
    node "$GUESSLESS/scripts/reproduce-check.mjs" docs/ evidence/
  env:
    GUESSLESS: ${{ github.workspace }}/guessless
```

# and MCP configs. Generated files are COMMITTED (per ruler's team guidance)
# so fresh clones and crew worktrees have guidance immediately; CI and the
# pre-commit hook fail on drift between .ruler/ sources and generated files.
default_agents = ["claude", "codex"]

[gitignore]
enabled = false

[skills]
enabled = true

[mcp]
enabled = true
merge_strategy = "merge"

[mcp_servers.grep]
url = "https://mcp.grep.app"

[mcp_servers.chrome-devtools]
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "chrome-devtools-mcp@1.5.0", "--headless", "--isolated"]

[agents.claude]
enabled = true
output_path = "CLAUDE.md"

[agents.codex]
enabled = true
output_path = "AGENTS.md"
